name: fire roasted meatballs
instructions:
Meatballs in a fire-roasted tomato sauce, served over pasta. Split off from the original master-ragu file (now master-bolognese.json) — the fire-roasted character + meatball shape distinguish this from the other ragu variants.

- Shape impossible meat into meatballs and brown in olive oil.
- Add FIRE ROASTED canned tomatoes (not regular — the fire-roasted character is the dish's signature), red wine vinegar, fennel seeds, bay leaf.
- Simmer until thickened.
- Toss with pasta.
notes:
=== FIRE-ROASTED TOMATOES ARE LOAD-BEARING ===

Regular canned tomatoes make a fine dish but not this dish. The smoky fire-roasted character is what makes this recipe distinct from the bolognese family (master-bolognese.json) and the mushroom eggplant ragus (mushroom-eggplant-ragu.json), all of which want regular canned tomatoes. If you're out of fire-roasted, save this recipe for another day rather than substituting.

=== MEATBALL SHAPE IS LOAD-BEARING ===

Impossible meat shaped into meatballs. The shaping matters — without the meatball format, this collapses into a generic vegan ragu with fire-roasted tomatoes. The distinct meatball-per-forkful texture IS the recipe.

=== FENNEL SEEDS + BAY LEAF ===

Both in the sauce. Fennel seeds are especially at home with the fire-roasted + meatball combination — classic italian-american meatball register.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- master-bolognese.json: bolognese family (Marcella beef; Nisha lentil+toasted-walnut). Different shape entirely — no fire-roasted, no meatballs.
- mushroom-eggplant-ragu.json: simpler mushroom+eggplant+onion sauté for pasta. Different protein slot, different tomato treatment.
- master-italian-tomato-sauce-and-pesto.json: the protein-free italian pasta-sauce side.
